project.name: shopledger
project.description: Internal wholesale and retail billing, inventory, and khata ledger for Corner Shop.

nodes.name: config.js
nodes.summary: Exports runtime port, shop identity, HSN-to-GST slabs, inventory defaults, and coupon definitions shared by the server and billing modules.

nodes.name: coupons.js
nodes.summary: Normalizes promotion codes, validates activation and minimum order amounts, and computes capped percentage or flat discounts. Exposes active promotions for the catalog API.

nodes.name: invoice.js
nodes.summary: Computes accountant invoice figures and renders printable HTML invoices with a ledger mismatch notice. Its independent tax and coupon calculation differs from the order pricing pipeline.

nodes.name: pricing.js
nodes.summary: Computes order and cart-preview totals by apportioning coupon discounts over line items, applying item-specific GST, and splitting tax into CGST and SGST. Returns detailed line breakdowns with rounded currency amounts.

nodes.name: tax.js
nodes.summary: Resolves item GST rates from explicit overrides, HSN slabs, or the default rate, and splits GST into CGST and SGST. Provides slab-percentage and currency-rounding helpers.

nodes.name: reports.js
nodes.summary: Defines dashboard and GST reconciliation APIs, server-side cart pricing previews, and keyed JSON export. Reads persisted product data before validating coupons and calculating preview totals.

nodes.name: dates.js
nodes.summary: Formats local dates as DD/MM/YYYY, converts HTML date input into that representation, and derives the April-to-March fiscal year. Date normalization preserves day-first strings rather than chronological sort keys.

nodes.name: inventory.js
nodes.summary: Calculates sellable stock after reservations, validates order quantities, deducts stock for committed orders, and summarizes stock health and valuation. Cancellation release currently looks up productId and reduces reservations rather than restoring physical stock.

nodes.name: ledger.js
nodes.summary: Maintains customer khata balances, enforces credit limits, reverses order debits, and records settlements. Settlement arithmetic adds the request amount before numeric coercion, so string inputs can concatenate.

nodes.name: orders.js
nodes.summary: Adds and finds orders, applies search/status/date filters, and coordinates cancellation with inventory release and credit reversal. Order dates and sorting use day-first date strings.

nodes.name: reports.js
nodes.summary: Aggregates dashboard revenue, taxes, discounts, order statuses, stock health, and khata receivables. Reconciles saved order totals against independently calculated invoice figures.

nodes.name: orders.js
nodes.summary: Defines order list/detail, create, and cancel API handlers mounted beneath /api. Order creation resolves catalog prices, validates stock and coupons, charges khata when selected, deducts stock, appends audit history, and saves the JSON database.

tour.title: Application Entry Point
tour.description: Start at server.js to see how ShopLedger serves its retail and wholesale billing interface, mounts four Express API routers, and renders printable invoices. The server exports its app independently of listening, while config.js supplies the port, shop identity, GST slabs, and coupon definitions used throughout the tour.
tour.languageLesson: CommonJS require() loads local modules, and require.main === module distinguishes running the server directly from importing its Express app.

tour.title: Browser Billing Workflow
tour.description: Follow the static interface served by the entry point into the POS, order register, khata, and audit tabs. app.js keeps cart state, renders the DOM, and calls the API through callback-based XMLHttpRequest helpers; index.html and the stylesheet provide its shared visual structure.

tour.title: Order Request Lifecycle
tour.description: Trace a browser order submission into the order router, which resolves authoritative catalog prices before validating stock and coupons, computing totals, and coordinating customer credit. The order service handles creation, filtering, and cancellation, while the product router supplies catalog records enriched with tax and sellable-stock information.

tour.title: Reusable Billing Rules
tour.description: The order flow and live preview share pricing.js, which distributes coupon discounts across lines and applies each item’s GST rate before rounding totals. Coupon eligibility and caps belong in coupons.js, and HSN slabs plus CGST/SGST splitting belong in tax.js; extend these reusable rules when changing billing behavior.

tour.title: Stock and Customer Credit
tour.description: After pricing, inventory.js checks sellable stock and deducts committed quantities, while ledger.js applies khata charges, credit limits, reversals, and settlements. Cancellation and customer payments cross these boundaries, so inspect the current inventory-release mismatch and string settlement arithmetic before extending those workflows.

tour.title: Invoices and Reconciliation
tour.description: Printable invoices run a separate calculation path in invoice.js, which can disagree with the order totals computed earlier. reports.js exposes these discrepancies alongside revenue, stock, and receivable summaries, making reconciliation a useful place to inspect the impact of pricing changes.

tour.title: Persistence and Validation
tour.description: All order, stock, and customer changes ultimately pass through store.js, which synchronously reads and rewrites the entire JSON database and maintains audit history without transactions. Inspect db.json for the persisted collections and dates.js for day-first date handling, then use package.json to run npm start; npm test is a deliberately failing placeholder, and no build or lint scripts are configured.
